Issue Number: close #47400 

Problem Summary:

### What changed and how does it work?

Ensure that the cardinality estimate does not go below 1. As the estimate approaches zero, then all plans are inexpensive which makes it difficult for the optimizer to differentiate the plan choices.

issue_context.title: planner: zero estimation result if all values are in TopN
comments:
the related code about this is as follows
```
	// 3. use uniform distribution assumption for the rest (even when this value is not covered by the range of stats)
	histNDV := float64(c.Histogram.NDV - int64(c.TopN.Num()))
	if histNDV <= 0 {
		return 0, nil
	}
	return c.Histogram.notNullCount() / histNDV, nil
```

in first case, since topN is collected, and it is overlapped with the NDV indication in Histogram, so the computation here is meaningless, leading `histNDV := float64(c.Histogram.NDV - int64(c.TopN.Num()))` = `2-2` = 0

in the second case, since topN is not collected,  `histNDV := float64(c.Histogram.NDV - int64(c.TopN.Num()))` = `2-0` = 2, and the `Histogram.notNullCount()` is 2 as well , causing the returned value as `2/2` = 1

review_comments: I guess we should put this above those `fix` constants instead of the license header.
Does this mean we will always enable this optimization? So this fix control is for the users who want to use the old behavior, am I understand it correctly?
I found it in the document PR.
